what_happened: Job 20261030-060843-f4s2 (code job: add a reading check requiring gate order, reuse, record kind and direct checks) failed in planning, before any code was written. After the last round (5 of 5) the critic still said the plan needed revising. The critic found most of the plan matched the code. One major finding remained: the dependents list leaves out the `athena check-reading` command in athena-cli/src/main.rs (check_reading_command and its tests). That command calls check_reading_text, and the refusal-rule replay runs it on both builds, so criterion 4 depends on it. Four minor findings and one nit were also raised. verify.rs is not a listed deliverable. The plan says no step can measure the real refused share, but the in-loop replay does. The skip-switch and helper rule only catches literal English words. The `Direct check:` clause is demanded even on routine criteria. The record-tag probe parses serde error text. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Planning checks that named files and helpers exist, but nothing makes the plan trace every caller and consumer of a new reading-refusal rule. Here the `athena check-reading` command is the binary the replay runs on both builds, and the plan's dependents list missed it. The rule's matching was also designed from the reading's wording, not recorded real criteria. Planning has fixed rounds, keeps no partial plan and has no repair step, so a single major finding that only needs a dependents entry and a test command still loses all planning spend.
other_causes: The plan treated the real refused share as unmeasurable, though the in-loop replay measures it during the producer run, so the plan did not say what the producer does with that result.
The request is broad (gate order, reuse, record kind, direct check in one rule), which gives more surfaces to miss.
The rule demands a `Direct check:` clause on routine criteria, so it would over-refuse ordinary readings. That is the false-refusal pattern this class describes.
open_hypotheses: Whether a repair step for mechanical omissions, such as a missing dependents entry, would have let this plan pass in round 5.
Whether the reading itself should have listed the check-reading command and verify.rs as deliverables.
contradictions: The critic judged the overall design sound and most plan claims matched the code, so this is not a wrong design. The only major finding was a mechanical omission.
prevention: Add a planning step that, for any new reading-refusal rule, lists every caller of the checking function by search, including CLI commands the replay invokes, and requires each in the dependents list with a test. Also add a mechanical repair round, after the last critic round, for findings that only need a dependents or deliverables entry. The plan should be run against recorded real criteria and readings, not wording-derived examples.
proposed_request:
Add a reading check to Athena that requires gate order, reuse, record kind and a direct check for behavior criteria. Acceptance:
- The plan lists every caller of check_reading_text as a dependent, including the `athena check-reading` command in crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs (check_reading_command and its tests at about lines 1265-1425), and names the command that runs its tests.
- crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs is a listed deliverable.
- The `Direct check:` clause is required only for criteria that change code behavior. Routine criteria such as 'fmt, clippy and test pass' are exempt.
- The skip-switch and internal-helper rule also catches identifier forms such as skip_x or a snake_case helper name, with tests.
- Record kind is read from the existing schema accessors on AnyRecord and HistoryRecord, not from serde error text.
- The plan says what the producer does with the in-loop replay's measured refused share.
- The rule is run over recorded past readings, and the refused share is reported.
- fmt, clippy and test pass.
- CHANGELOG.md has an entry.
